title: Solve a bare linear equation for x
subtitle: Linear equations in one variable · 38 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **38 of the official questions in Linear equations in one variable are this one** — 26 Easy, 7 Medium, 5 Hard.
It is bottom-heavy, which makes it cheap points. Secure it early.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- You see one equation with only x in it (sometimes fractions, decimals, or a common factor like a group in parentheses on both terms).
- It asks for x itself, or asks which equation is equivalent to it.
- The answer choices are plain numbers, or it's a grid-in.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) If the same grouped factor appears in every term, factor it out first; if there are fractions, multiply through by the common denominator.
- 2) Move the x-terms to one side and the constants to the other.
- For 'which is equivalent', do the operation that turns the given equation into the form the choices are written in.

sections.heading: Where Desmos fits
body: Type the equation exactly as given.
Desmos draws a vertical line at the solution, and you can tap it to read x.
You can also graph y = left side and y = right side and read the x-coordinate of the intersection.
This is fastest when the equation has fractions or decimals.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: The wrong choices are what you get from a sign slip when you move a term across, from subtracting the coefficient when you should divide by it, or from the solution of a similar equation with one sign flipped.
Plug your answer back in to check.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.

The wrong choices are what you get from a sign slip when you move a term across, from subtracting the coefficient when you should divide by it, or from the solution of a similar equation with one sign flipped.
Plug your answer back in to check.
